newsitem.title: USA: Centennial to restate losses to 1994, stock plunges.
newsitem.headline: Centennial to restate losses to 1994, stock plunges.

text.p: Centennial Technologies Inc., which has been hit by allegations of insider trading against its former chief executive, said Thursday it would restate its financial results and expected to report losses for the past 3-1/2 years.
The news sent Centennial's stock plunging just two days after its value tripled on news that the maker of personal computer memory cards had record sales last week.
Centennial -- the best performer on the New York Stock Exchange last year -- lost two-thirds of its value, falling $9.75 to $5. It was the most active issue on the NYSE in early afternoon trading.

The stock had tripled in value on Tuesday, surging $10.25 to $14.75 after Lawrence Ramaekers, the interim chief executive to replace fired founder and Chief Executive Emanuel Pinez, told Reuters the company had record sales last week.
Trading in Centennial was halted on Wednesday.
Centennial said it would restate financial results for fiscal 1994, 1995 and 1996 and the first two quarters of fiscal 1997 and it expected to report "material cumulative losses" for the periods.

"The anticipated restatements will relate both to the company's operations, including an inventory write-off and sales reversals, and to non-operating losses attributable to an anticipated write-down of the carrying value of certain investments," the company said.
Centennial, based in Billerica, Mass., said it would release the revised figures in six to 12 weeks.
It said the special committee it set up to investigate the matter was still probing the activities of Pinez.
The company fired Pinez on Feb. 11 after he admitted to the special committee that he falsified Centennial's sales to meet Wall Street expectations, according to court documents.
Pinez was charged by the Securities and Exchange Commission and the U.S. Attorney's office in Boston with insider trading and has been held in a Plymouth, Mass. jail.

On Feb. 18 the company said it expected to restate its financial results for fiscal 1996, ended last June 30, and for the first two quarters of fiscal 1997. It said that "certain financial records of the company appear to have been falsified.
